definitions.bindingStatus: Root must bind the actual committed source candidate and actual clean-source --keep output before execution. These definitions bind current bytes only.

controls.discriminator: US table NYDFS literal due-date case and persisted signed NYDFS due72 case

discriminatingCases.fullName: stored signed incident clock events persists a genuine signed row and verifies after closing and reopening SQLite
discriminatingCases.oracle: The returned NYDFS dueTs must equal literal T+72*HOUR. With this source delta the static arithmetic is T+71*HOUR, a one-hour difference. Earlier genuine-signature/persisted-event assertions precede this due-date assertion.

discriminatingCases.fullName: US financial clock literals at a fixed date nydfs-500-17-notice has an independent literal due-date expectation
discriminatingCases.oracle: The expected NYDFS value is written in the test table as T+72*HOUR, independent of the product clock table.

controls.masking: Additional notification/status/due-date and earlier-trigger cases may fail. Count only actual body failures. A first assertion inside a case can mask later expectations; no predicted global failure order or failure count.
controls.preserved: Only the INCIDENT_DETERMINATION72-hour row changes; other72-hour clocks and all guards remain unchanged.

controls.discriminator: cold edited timestamp is refused by event id after valid original signature proof
controls.limit: Use timestamp corruption, not the already-red station-filter case, for causal sensitivity. The independent Node verification still detects edited bytes; only loader refusal is removed.

discriminatingCases.fullName: stored signed incident clock events cold edited timestamp is refused by event id after valid original signature proof
discriminatingCases.oracle: The original row independently verifies, the cold-copy ts edit T→T+1 independently fails Node verification, and the loader must throw the event-specific signature refusal. The edited timestamp still satisfies the semantic bounds, so those guards should not mask signature-check removal.

controls.masking: The original-database positive assertion at228 is after the expected refusal and is masked if toThrow fails. Station-tamper and wrong-key cases may also fail; retain them but do not count the station test as a separate map-before-filter control. Independent Node verification remains intact.
controls.preserved: Only the loader signature-refusal if block is removed; event digests, record signing, independent test verifier, map-before-filter and semantic guards stay unchanged. This deliberately leaves an unused import; mutation execution is source-mode sensitivity, not a typecheck/build qualification.

controls.discriminator: rejects a pre-creation notice even when its trigger has not started, with no appended row
controls.limit: NOTIFIED for an unstarted NYDFS clock has no trigger guard to mask removal; ordinary backdated TRIGGER retains defense in attachRegulatoryClocks and alone would be an inconclusive guard control.

discriminatingCases.fullName: stored signed incident clock events rejects a pre-creation notice even when its trigger has not started, with no appended row
discriminatingCases.oracle: The actual record call uses NOTIFIED/NYDFS at T-1 with no INCIDENT_DETERMINATION. Removing only the admission guard should allow the ordinary sign/insert path: attachRegulatoryClocks returns NOT_STARTED when triggerTs is null before its satisfied-before-trigger check. The store schema does not add a createdTs constraint.

controls.masking: The empty-row assertion at174 is after the failed toThrow and must not be credited if masked. Retained observations/SQLite could establish a real append separately, but do not infer that measurement from a nonzero exit. An ordinary pre-creation TRIGGER retains the attachRegulatoryClocks trigger guard and is not by itself a discriminator.
controls.preserved: Only the event.ts<incident.createdTs guard is removed; timestamp finiteness, future skew, known station/clock, signature, duplicate-notice and trigger consistency remain unchanged.

phaseContract: Root alone mutates a physically owned freshQ source file after verifying the exact baseline hash and the one literal occurrence. Never substitute R forQ.

Retain original tests, config, global/per-file guards, deadlines and owned child lifecycle. The R Vitest runner is explicitly borrowed; --root must select the actual freshQ and source paths must be recorded.

For each distinct control, retain a complete unchanged baseline, mutant and byte-exact restored phase with actual statuses and closure; no automatic replay of completed phases. Root may bind shared prior baseline only if that attribution is explicit.

Baseline/restored require all registered cases passed with zero errors/pending/todo and normal owned closure. A mutant requires actual discriminating body failures or an explicitly reported survivor; setup/hook/timeout/unhandled/late-close/process uncertainty is not a kill.

No compiler, import adapter, test edits, filter, deadline extension, source repair or shared-source mutation is proposed. Preserve complete raw/observer/log/inputs/closure and any failed fixture observations.

mixedExecutionBoundary.sourceMode: The event/table originals and new event tests import TS source through Vitest. Causal sensitivity belongs to those actual loaded source paths.
mixedExecutionBoundary.compiledSurfaces: incidentClockSurfaces.test.ts resolves its physical checkout and uses dist/cli.js plus dist incident/API/MCP modules. TS-only mutations leave those freshly built compiled children byte-exact. Their pass results remain real compiled baseline/compatibility observations and must not be called compiled-mutant sensitivity.
mixedExecutionBoundary.independentChildren: Parent is Node built-ins only; child cold init/seed avoid a parent SQLite pool. HTTP is an owned loopback route fixture without outer authn; MCP uses real linked SDK transports, not external network auth.
mixedExecutionBoundary.fixtureRetention: Event fixtures close SQLite and delete successes; failed bodies retain observations. Retained public files must be inspected before any extra append/effect claims. Surface fixtures retain public observations and child/stream/PID closure. No private key/secret config body is to be published.

fourthControl.recommendation: Do not add a fourth runtime.
fourthControl.reason: The original station-hiding baseline already failed at238:105 on the old pre-filter source and passed after the exact repair. That is direct regression sensitivity for map-before-filter. Restoring the old filter again would duplicate this proof rather than supply one of the three required specification controls.
fourthControl.ifLaterRequested: Keep it a separate named regression control with original RED/post-repair attribution; do not count M2 station failures as this distinct source recipe.

limits: All predictions are static hypotheses. Actual fresh registration, failure values, masking, survivors and closure supersede them.

These three controls test implementation sensitivity; they do not provide legal/expert approval, whole-suite/full-build mutant proof, hosted execution, independent person identity or formal P117 Done.
Current repaired source and existing legal/content/source caveats remain unchanged.
